Far Cry 5 is a dynamic first-person shooter with an open world, developed by Ubisoft. The story takes place in the fictional Hope County, Montana, USA, where a religious cult called "The Project at Eden's Gate," led by Joseph Seed, has seized power.
The game's main strength lies in its vast, beautiful, and lively open world. The landscapes — from dense forests to mountainous regions — look stunning. It's enjoyable to simply drive around the county, explore it, and encounter unexpected events.
The gameplay is diverse: assaulting outposts, rescuing hostages, hunting, fishing, and engaging in large-scale shootouts. The system of hiring companions adds tactical depth: you can gather your own team of allies, each with unique abilities.
The story touches on rather dark themes, such as fanaticism, propaganda, and the abuse of power, but it's presented with the series’ characteristic touch of absurdity. Some characters are very memorable thanks to their vivid development.
On the downside: after several hours, the gameplay can start to feel repetitive, and missions often follow a similar structure. Some mechanics seem designed to artificially stretch out the game's length. Additionally, many players found the ending controversial and emotionally divisive.
Conclusion:
Far Cry 5 is a spectacular and gripping game with a beautiful open world and engaging action. If you enjoy shooters and value freedom of choice, it's definitely worth trying, despite some flaws in storytelling and mission design.

Beautiful game and extremely fun to play. I played with my brother in co-op mode and it was the most fun I had in a co-op game in a long time. It stands up even as a solo play-through game. You can take your time and enjoy the mundane things like fishing, driving around, hunting, and exploring OR you can finish the main quest line while still experiencing a portion of these things.

Pros:
+ Combat is smooth and fun. Shooting is familiar so you can carry over any FPS skills you may think you have :D no flame
+ Driving is fun
+ Nice selection of weapons to choose from and customize
+ Very interesting story
+ Well written antagonist
+ Good amount of side quests and mundane things to do just to chill out and listen to music (i.e. fishing, driving cars/boats)
+ Co-op is a really nice addition

Cons:
- Wish there were more weapons to choose from
- More weapon customization would be nice
- Co-op play with up to 4 players would've been really nice for bigger friend groups

As other reviews have said, its like a Far Cry game, but with a shitty story, shitty characters, shitty antagonists, and a pretty lackluster ending. If you are looking at getting into the Far Cry franchise, 3 and 4 are fantastic. If you have played Far Cry in the past, and want to experience this one, buy it on sale and set your expectations low.

The open world component was fantastic, so it was enjoyable from a gameplay perspective, but the story gets rammed down your throat, and detracts from the rest of the game.

Repetitive gameplay loop (three areas, three times the same).
Cutscenes interrupting said repetitive gameplay loop out of nowhere in the most nonsensical way possible.
Shallow and rather unlikeable characters (some npcs for sidequests entertaining though).
Shoddy written ending.
Co-op progress only saved for host (forcing the non host to either use "prestige" weapons ... or base stuff)

Some side activities were nice though (looting stashes, climbing mountains, fishing)

Best avoided like rabies.

Finally, Ubisoft made a competitor to Manhunt.

This game kept me invested for quite a long time. I really enjoyed the gunplay and the variety of weapons and equipment, although it's clear that some options are much better than others, which means you end up using only a few of them most of the time.

The driving is arcade-like at best, but it didn’t ruin the experience for me. Still, I mostly used vehicles only when necessary, preferring fast travel whenever possible.

The prepper stash “puzzles” are very simple, but I didn’t mind that and actually appreciated them for what they were. I also liked the Arcade mode with community-created maps.

The fishing minigame feels a bit underdeveloped, though it still worked as a nice little distraction.

Overall, I believe the game is better than the sum of its parts. However, if it were more complex and offered more varied activities, it could move from being just an OK/fun game to something truly special.

I went back to gaming after a 10 year break. I got recommended Far Cry 5. Unfortunately, I felt disappointed with almost everything. Graphics should impress, but didn't. I can't put my finger on it, but there was something that just felt off. Everything else was just like 10 years ago. Like save points. I find nothing more irritating in games than being forced to play the same scene over and over again, instead of using regular saving and loading. It seems like the lazy and boring route to make things tougher.
Overall Far Cry 5 felt like an old, stupid FPS. Scripted, repeated, uncanny valley-faced NPC appearing from nowhere, a very limited AI, all bad guys wearing the same face and driving the same cars, using the exact same looped walking paths, voices was reused again and again.
This game felt bad from the first second and I could not shrug that feeling off, so after just three hours of gameplay I uninstalled the game and I will never play it again. What a waste of time. Thank god I only payed $9 and not $59.99 (!) - that would have been outright depressing.

Ever since Far Cry 3, sneaking my way through outposts eliminating enemies one by one has been one of my favorite things to do in video games. I’m happy to report that systematically taking down murderous thugs is just as fun in rural America as it is in the Himalayas, and that Far Cry 5 is another great game in the open-world series Ubisoft seems most willing to have fun with. It may be playing a familiar tune, but all of these combat, physics, and wildlife systems all mix together to create unexpected moments of intense and hilarious action.

This time around you play as a sheriff’s deputy, part of a task force sent into the fictional Hope County, Montana. Rural America may not be quite as exotic or exciting a playground as a tropical island or a secluded mountain, but it’s a gigantic open world where things are constantly blowing up, wild animals are pouncing, and a never-ending supply of cultists are lining up to be your target practice. The mountains, valleys, plains, forests, rivers, lakes, and caves of Hope County make it a place where there’s never a dull moment.
